_readme: THE TWO-ENTRY PATTERN. Entry 1 ("broker") STARTS the broker process and bridges it to this host over stdio. Entry 2 ("scene-editor") ATTACHES to the listener entry 1 already opened. There is exactly one broker process.
Replace /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO with the real path. MCP hosts do not expand ~, $HOME or relative paths, and the working directory a host spawns a server in is not the one you are reading this from.

ENTRY 1, why MCP_BROKER_STDIO_PROVIDER must be "_all": the stdio bridge gates every frame, initialize included, on the target slot being occupied. Pin it to a real slot and the handshake fails whenever the host starts before that provider connects, which for a browser-hosted provider is every single time; the host then marks the server failed and stops retrying. "_all" is occupied from broker startup, answers initialize itself, unions every opted-in provider, and pushes notifications/tools/list_changed as providers join, so a provider that appears an hour later still shows up live.

ENTRY 2, why it must not spawn anything: a second `command` entry running @cyanmycelium/mcp-broker starts a SECOND broker. It either dies with EADDRINUSE on the port entry 1 holds, or, if you give it another port, comes up as a completely separate broker sharing no slots with the first, so its tools are permanently missing and nothing says why. Entry 2 is a URL.

Entry 2 is optional. Add it only when you want one slot to have its own identity in the host: its own permission prompts, its own tool namespace, and unprefixed tool names. Through entry 1 the same tools are already reachable as "<slot>-<tool>".
